chai.stage.s1.title: Define the problem & plan
chai.stage.s1.blurb: Agree on the clinical or operational problem, confirm AI is the right tool, and name who is accountable before anything is built or bought.
chai.item.s1-1: Problem statement and target outcome agreed with clinical and operational stakeholders
chai.item.s1-2: Current-state or root-cause analysis shows AI is an appropriate intervention, not just a possible one
chai.item.s1-3: Success measures and a baseline to compare against are defined
chai.item.s1-4: Affected patient populations identified, including groups at risk of being underserved or harmed
chai.item.s1-5: Potential harms and failure modes listed, with severity and likelihood
chai.item.s1-6: Accountable owner, governance body, and decision rights named
chai.item.s1-7: Data needs, privacy, consent, and regulatory constraints scoped
chai.stage.s2.title: Design the AI system
chai.stage.s2.blurb: Specify how the system fits into care: who uses it, where in the workflow, what it outputs, and what happens when it is wrong.
chai.item.s2-1: End users took part in workflow and interface design
chai.item.s2-2: Intended use, users, and care setting documented, with out-of-scope uses listed
chai.item.s2-3: Subgroups and fairness criteria for evaluation pre-specified
chai.item.s2-4: Decision thresholds defined and clinically justified
chai.item.s2-5: Human oversight and override path designed into the workflow
chai.item.s2-6: Pathway for reporting safety issues and harms drafted, naming who reports to whom
chai.item.s2-7: Threat model, access controls, and data flows designed
chai.stage.s3.title: Engineer the AI solution
chai.stage.s3.blurb: Build or configure the model with traceable data and documented choices, so the assessment stage has something it can verify.
chai.item.s3-1: Data provenance and known data limitations documented
chai.item.s3-2: Demographic and socio-demographic make-up of development data characterized
chai.item.s3-3: Bias mitigation approach chosen and documented
chai.item.s3-4: Data quality checks and handling of missing data documented
chai.item.s3-5: Version control in place for datasets, code, and model artifacts
chai.item.s3-6: De-identification or other privacy-enhancing techniques applied where appropriate
chai.item.s3-7: People responsible for monitoring data and model behavior designated
chai.stage.s4.title: Assess
chai.stage.s4.blurb: Validate the solution locally before patients are exposed to it. Record key metrics below; they flow into the model card.
chai.item.s4-1: Performance validated on local data representative of the deployment population
chai.item.s4-2: Performance compared across demographic subgroups, with gaps explained
chai.item.s4-4: Silent (shadow) evaluation run in the live environment
chai.item.s4-6: Explanations of outputs are suited to the intended users
chai.item.s4-7: Security review or vendor security assessment completed
chai.item.s4-8: Safety reporting pathway updated with what assessment revealed
chai.stage.s5.title: Pilot
chai.stage.s5.blurb: Run a small, time-boxed pilot to learn whether the solution helps in real care, for whom, and at what cost to staff.
chai.item.s5-1: Pilot scope, sites, duration, and stop rules defined
chai.item.s5-2: Usability and workflow fit assessed with frontline users
chai.item.s5-3: Real-world effect on outcomes or process measured against baseline
chai.item.s5-4: Pilot results checked for differences across patient groups
chai.item.s5-5: Adverse events and near misses tracked and reviewed
chai.item.s5-6: Users trained, and the approach to patient disclosure decided
chai.stage.s6.title: Deploy & monitor
chai.stage.s6.blurb: Scale up with monitoring, change control, and a plan for when to retrain or retire.
chai.item.s6-1: Performance and drift monitoring live, with alert thresholds and an owner
chai.item.s6-2: Subgroup performance monitored on an ongoing basis
chai.item.s6-3: Audit schedule and change control set, with a revised model card for each version
chai.item.s6-4: Incident response, rollback, and retirement criteria documented
chai.item.s6-5: Access reviews and security patching scheduled
chai.item.s6-6: Value to patients and staff re-evaluated periodically
chai.gate.A.title: Checkpoint A
chai.gate.A.help: Is the problem worth solving with AI, and is the plan sound enough to start design?
chai.gate.B.title: Checkpoint B
chai.gate.B.help: Has local assessment shown the solution is safe, effective, and fair enough to expose a small group of patients to it?
chai.gate.C.title: Checkpoint C
chai.gate.C.help: Did the pilot show real benefit without unacceptable harm or disparity?
chai.gate.D.title: Checkpoint D
chai.gate.D.help: Based on monitoring, should the solution continue as is, change, or be retired? Record a new review each cycle; the next due date is set from it.
